svg.text: The Jacobi Eigensolver on the Jig
Find the flat plane the drilled holes lie in — the direction they barely spread along is the plate's normal.
λ₃
most spread
λ₂
n̂
λ₁ · the plate's normal
Three perpendicular axes fall out — the two
big ones lie in the plate, the small one (n̂)
points out of it. That's the normal.
Spin the spread matrix until it's diagonal:
covariance of the holes
rotate
the three spreads (eigenvalues)
Three steps
Measure the spread
Build the 3×3 covariance M of the hole
positions — how they scatter in x, y, z.
Spin it to diagonal (the Jacobi part)
Rotate one plane at a time to zero an
off-diagonal, until all are ≈ 0.
θ = (aᶲᶲ − aᶫᶫ) / (2 aᶫᶲ)
a few sweeps · stop when Σ|off-diag| < 1e−18
Read the axes
The diagonal holds the three spreads λ,
each with a direction (its eigenvector):
• smallest λ → n̂, the plate normal
• other two → the in-plane layout axes u, v
Why it wins: the holes barely spread out of their
plane, so the smallest-spread direction IS the normal.
